rules: CHEMICAL covers explicitly named chemicals and drugs; DISEASE covers explicitly named diseases and pathological conditions, including named adverse effects.
Do not restrict diseases to conditions caused by a chemical in the same sentence; this task is entity recognition, not relation extraction.
Chemical names, disease names and their separately occurring abbreviations each need the correct occurrence. Do not merge chemical and disease labels.
Disease subtype or anatomical modifiers may be part of a disease name. Preserve named clinical conditions; do not mechanically label every measurement, symptom word or general drug reference.
